title: Kenyan Full Breakfast
community: The complete Kenyan morning — traditional and modern in one
author: Mama Wanjiru
desc: Kenyan Full Breakfast — a comprehensive morning meal combining traditional Kenyan elements (uji wa wimbi, boiled arrowroot, sweet potato) with modern additions (eggs, sausage, mandazi, chai). The breakfast that honours both sides of Kenya's food culture.
longDesc: The full Kenyan breakfast is an exercise in cultural synthesis — the traditional breakfast of arrowroot, sweet potato, and millet porridge sits alongside the modern additions of fried eggs, sausage, and toast. Together they tell the complete story of Kenyan morning food.
ingredients: 1 cup uji wa wimbi (millet porridge — see KEN191)
steps: Prepare uji wa wimbi as per KEN191.
Boil arrowroot and sweet potato until tender.
Make masala chai and fresh juice.
Arrange traditional and modern elements on a large warm plate in sections.
Serve all together — the traditional and modern side by side.
chefTips: Warm everything before plating — nothing should be served cold.
The uji can be made ahead and reheated.
The arrowroot and sweet potato are at their best served immediately after boiling.
commonMistakes: Too little food — the full Kenyan breakfast should be generous.
cookingScience: The full Kenyan breakfast is nutritionally complete — the millet porridge provides complex carbohydrates and iron; eggs provide complete protein; sweet potato provides beta-carotene; arrowroot provides easily digestible starch; beans provide plant protein and fibre.
sustainabilityTips: The traditional elements (arrowroot, sweet potato, millet porridge, mandazi) are entirely locally produced with zero food miles.
healthBenefits: Traditional elements provide iron, calcium, and beta-carotene.
culturalNote: The full Kenyan breakfast is Kenya's morning in one plate — traditional heritage foods alongside modern additions, honouring both where Kenya has come from and where it is going. No other country has quite this combination at the breakfast table.
